DATE
Wednesday, April 29, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
President and Chief Executive Officer — Maria Black
Chief Financial Officer — Peter Hadley
Operator
TAKEAWAYS
Total Revenue Growth
-- 7% increase for the quarter, driven by both Employer Services and Professional Employer Organization segments.
Adjusted EBIT Margin Expansion
-- Improved by 80 basis points, attributed to operational productivity and client funds interest revenue growth.
Adjusted EPS Growth
-- 10% gain, outpacing management’s prior expectations.
Employer Services (ES) Revenue
-- Rose 7% on a reported basis and 5% on an organic constant currency basis, with foreign exchange contributing close to 2 percentage points.
PEO Revenue (excluding zero-margin pass-throughs)
-- Increased 5%, offset by 7% total PEO revenue growth which included zero-margin pass-throughs.
ES Margins
-- Gained 130 basis points, primarily due to productivity improvements and higher client funds interest revenue.
PEO Margins
-- Declined by 120 basis points, driven by growth in zero-margin pass-throughs, increased SUI costs, and higher selling expenses.
Employer Services Retention Rate
-- Achieved a record quarterly high, with broad-based strength cited across international, compliance, and small business segments.
Client Satisfaction
-- "Overall client satisfaction levels reached new record highs for a third quarter."
New Business Bookings (ES)
-- Delivered solid growth, especially in international and compliance solutions; pipeline remains healthy entering the fourth quarter.
PACE per Control Growth (ES)
-- Remained at 1% for the third quarter; fiscal-year outlook unchanged at approximately 1%.
Average Client Funds Balances Growth
-- Up 9% in the quarter, with full-year forecast raised to approximately 6% growth and average yield expected at about 3.4%.
Client Funds Interest Revenue
-- Forecast midpoint raised by $25 million, now expected in the range of $1.34 billion to $1.35 billion for the year.
Share Repurchase Activity
-- Management noted a "meaningful increase" in repurchases year-to-date, with plans to continue at or above current elevated levels through the balance of the year and fiscal 2027.
Full-Year Outlook Revisions
-- Consolidated revenue growth guidance lifted to 6%-7%; adjusted EBIT margin expansion forecast increased to 70–80 basis points; adjusted EPS growth now expected at 10%-11%.
AI and Automation Efficiency Gains
-- Cited use of ADP Assist agents and Smart Actions, including a reported 80% reduction in time spent on common HR actions and a 30-minute savings per payroll run via AI-powered tools.
Lyric HCM Platform Impact
-- Reduced recruiting process steps from 23 to 8, and enabled a 71% leaner payroll operations model for client case studies noted in the call.
ES New Business Mix
-- "About 50%" of new bookings from new client logos and 50% from existing clients (upsells and expanded offerings).
Pricing Contribution
-- Pricing contributed approximately 130 basis points to revenue growth, exceeding the prior goal of 100 basis points.
International Performance
-- Highlighted as a source of strong growth and strategic bookings momentum.
M&A Commentary
-- Management confirmed ongoing pursuit of small acquisitions, with recent deals in Mexico and Nordic countries, but no major transactions announced.
Operational Deployment of GenAI
-- 20% of total service operations now on the new internal GenAI platform as of March, targeting 40%+ by the end of fiscal 2026.
PEO Average Worksite Employee Growth
-- Maintained at 2% for the quarter, with same figure forecasted for the full fiscal year.
Tax Rate
-- Full-year effective tax rate remains at approximately 23%.
ES Revenue Model Mix
-- Management stated a "higher propensity" for seat-based billing models, especially in mid-market and up-market segments, with other revenue sources in Retirement and Insurance Services.
ES Client Contact Reduction
-- Client contacts down 8% year over year for small business clients, the busiest quarter of the year, powered by AI and platform investments.

RISKS
PEO margins decreased 120 basis points in Q3 due to 0 margin pass-through growth, higher SUI costs, and higher selling expenses.
Employer Services new business bookings guidance for full-year maintained at a wide 4%-7% range, with management explicitly citing "ongoing macro uncertainty" as limiting visibility on ultimate outcomes.
Management stated, "ES [ pays ] per control growth remained at 1% for the third quarter," with guidance for similar growth, suggesting muted organic headcount expansion within client base.
Guidance cautioned that fourth quarter foreign exchange benefit to revenue is expected to moderate, so there will be a little bit less benefit from FX on the revenue side, reducing prior FX tailwind and posing a potential headwind for reported growth and margins.

reported quarterly financial results and raised full-year guidance for revenue, adjusted EBIT margin, and adjusted EPS due to outperformance in both key segments and continued client fund balance growth. Strategic initiatives in AI and platform investments drove operational efficiency, resulting in noticeable reductions in client contacts and measurable savings for clients using new AI-driven tools. The Lyric HCM platform continued to gain traction, offering time and process savings to enterprise clients and supporting expansion into new addressable markets. International and compliance offerings contributed significantly to bookings strength, and record-high client retention and satisfaction metrics underpinned management’s confidence heading into the final quarter. Management signaled that share repurchases will remain elevated, while price increases have contributed meaningfully to top-line growth.
Management increased its midpoint guidance by $25 million for both client funds interest revenue and the net impact from its extended investment strategy, reflecting continued favorable trends in client fund balances and yields.
The mix between new client wins and upsells for Employer Services revenue remained balanced at 50/50, establishing a consistent pattern for sales momentum and pipeline composition.
More than 200 new HR-related compliance laws were enacted in the U.S. so far this year, and management linked rising regulatory demands to increased demand for ADP’s compliance solutions.
Senior management highlighted continued internal deployment of Generative AI, now operating in 20% of service operations, and plans to accelerate this to over 40%, with ensuing productivity and margin benefits expected.
While the company cited improved R&D efficiency from AI, quarter-to-quarter R&D expenses may fluctuate due to accounting adjustments and reallocation of expenses, not just operational changes.
Returns from price increases rose to 130 basis points contributing to overall revenue, with both client satisfaction and retention also reaching record levels, suggesting little customer pushback on price.
Enterprise traction for Lyric HCM was attributed to its flexible architecture addressing new use cases, including deployment alongside other HCM platforms and expansion via system integrators.
Management reported that PEO segment margin pressure stemmed from high variable sales compensation, increased SUI revenues (at lower margin), and less favorable workers’ comp reserve releases compared to the prior year.
The company maintained a consistent approach to value-based pricing, capturing efficiency gains from AI through overall product margin and retention rather than specific usage-based fees.
Management reiterated the competitive environment remains relatively competitive, with no notable change in pressure from digital native or AI-driven entrants, despite ongoing seasonal competition in the second half.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
Employer Services (ES)
: ADP segment delivering payroll, HR, compliance, and benefit administration solutions for enterprise and SMB clients.
Professional Employer Organization (PEO)
: Segment providing co-employment HR outsourcing, including benefits, payroll, and compliance for small to mid-sized clients.
PACE per Control
: KPI representing the number of employee paychecks processed per ADP client, serving as a proxy for employment levels within client companies.
Client Funds Interest Revenue
: Income earned on float from holding client payroll and tax funds before remittance to employees and taxing authorities.
SUI Revenues
: Statutory unemployment insurance-related revenues managed by PEO on behalf of client companies, with generally lower margin.
ADP Assist
: AI-powered suite of agents and workflow automation tools designed to improve operational efficiency and accuracy for payroll and HR functions.
Lyric HCM
: Enterprise platform utilizing AI and flexible architecture to streamline global payroll, recruitment, and HR processes.
Zero-margin pass-throughs
: Revenues recorded for pass-through amounts (such as taxes and insurance premiums) with no profit margin for the provider.
